Static Ads Generator · the change

Same brand. Same brief. Two ways to make the ad.

Every ad on the left came out of the current generator for Trade With The Pros. Every ad on the right is the same concept, rebuilt the new way — the concept decided first, then the type and logos set by hand in code, and the image model kept away from anything it garbles. Judge it side by side.

Current generator — template + one-shot image model Concept-first — strategy, then a deterministic render
01

Why the current output looks AI-made

These are not one-off glitches. The same failures repeat across the set, because they all come from the same place.

Invented brand text

A screen in the render reads “ASA1” — signage the model made up.

The headline, twice

Wordmark plus a giant repeat of the same name in the same frame.

Text baked into the image

Headlines melted into the pixels: soft, and impossible to edit later.

Clip-art problem icons

Stocky little illustrations that read as a template, not a concept.

Off-brand CTA

A yellow button on a brand that is blue.

Uncanny, repeated faces

The same AI “trader” looking slightly different in every scene.

The root cause is one thing: the image model is asked to invent the concept, paint the scene, and set the type — all in a single shot. No tool does all three well at once, so the type garbles, the logo warps, and the concept defaults to whatever template was picked.

03

The change, in one line

Split the three jobs the image model was doing badly, and give each to the tool that does it well.

Concept

A Claude strategist pass decides the idea for this client — angle, format, headline, visual direction. The template library is a source of inspiration, not the ceiling.

Text + logos

Rendered deterministically in HTML and CSS. Always crisp, always the real logo, always editable — never touched by an image model.

Imagery

The image model only ever paints a scene — no text, no logos — and it is composited underneath the crisp layer.

The check before anything ships

The SongReels-style rigor, written down. Nothing goes out until every line is true.

  • One concept, one hook, one visual, one CTA — reads in under two seconds
  • Headline speaks to this audience’s urgency, not a generic pitch
  • All text is HTML-rendered and crisp — nothing baked into an image
  • The logo is real, composited, undistorted — no garbled brand text
  • Brand fonts and colours are correct, pulled from the Brand Brain
  • Every claim and number is real — nothing invented
  • No AI artifacts: no uncanny faces, no garbled UI
  • Not a near-duplicate of another ad in the set — a distinct concept, not a recolour

All of this runs in-house.

Claude for strategy, copy and the QA pass. A render engine for the crisp layer. An image model for scenes only. There is no external tool to depend on before we can put this in front of clients and sell it.
